Instrument the R code of the base packages of R

Source: R/base_r.R
instrument_base_r.Rd

Instruments the installed base packages (base, stats, utils, ...) of the running R, so that the R processes it starts save the counts of the code they run, in trace_dir or in the directory of the environment variable COVERAGE_DIR. The counts are collected by base_r_code_coverage(). This changes the library of the running R: undo it with uninstrument_base_r(). Use base_r_compiled_coverage() for its C and Fortran code.

Usage

instrument_base_r(
  source_dir,
  lib = R.home("library"),
  trace_dir = file.path(dirname(lib), "covr-traces"),
  packages = base_r_packages(lib),
  exclusions = base_r_exclusions(),
  cores = getOption("Ncpus", 1L)
)

Arguments

source_dir

The directory of the source of R, that R was built from.

lib

The library of the base packages of R.

trace_dir

The directory the counts are saved in, if the environment variable COVERAGE_DIR is not set when a process of R exits.

packages

The packages to instrument, which must include base, whose loader counts the code that runs and saves the counts.

exclusions

A named list of the functions not to instrument, by package, e.g. list(stats = "pbinom"). Use NULL to instrument all of them, which makes some of R's checks fail.

cores

The number of packages to instrument in parallel, in forked processes. Instrumenting byte-compiles the code, which takes long in a build of R without optimization, e.g. one built for the coverage of its compiled code.

Value

A list, invisibly, with:

  • packages: the packages that were instrumented.

  • excluded: the functions that were not instrumented, by package: those in exclusions and those with a constant or UseMethod() body.

  • no_srcref: the functions of base that are not measured, as their code differs from the source files, e.g. as it was created by other code.

  • uncompiled: the functions that could not be byte-compiled.

Details

Functions of base have no source references in a build of R, so they are read from the source files in source_dir, which are used for the functions whose code is the same as the installed one. Functions without source references are not measured.

Some functions are not instrumented, so they are not in the coverage, not even as code that never ran: the functions in exclusions (by default base_r_exclusions(), those whose code R's own checks inspect), and functions whose body is a constant or a call to UseMethod(), which have no code to cover and whose bodies code also compares. The default arguments of functions are not traced either, as R CMD check compares them with the documentation.

Requirements

  • Build R from source, with the environment variable R_KEEP_PKG_SOURCE=yes set so that the packages have source references.

  • Run instrument_base_r() with the R that is instrumented, e.g. the bin/Rscript of a build that is not installed, as the byte-code in the databases depends on the version of R. covr has to be installed in a library this R can use, e.g. with R_LIBS.

  • covr must stay installed at the same path while R is instrumented, as instrumented processes load the native code of covr from there.

  • This is only supported on Unix-alikes: forked processes of parallel::mclapply() save their counts as they exit.

Example workflow

# With R built from `R-devel` in `build`, and covr installed in `lib`, run
# this with `R_LIBS=lib build/bin/Rscript`:
library(covr)
instrument_base_r("R-devel", lib = "build/library", trace_dir = "traces")

# Then run the checks, saving the counts in `traces`:
#   COVERAGE_DIR=traces make check

cov <- base_r_code_coverage("traces", "R-devel")
report(cov)

# Restore R, with the same R as above
uninstrument_base_r(lib = "build/library")
